utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning to the technical booth, the interpreters. Good morning legal assistants and registrar. Good morning to the Office of the Prosecutor, Defence counsel, and General Krstic. We shall be continuing your testimony, and I wish to remind you that you are continuing to testify under oath, and please answer directly as much as possible the questions put to you by Mr. Petrusic. If he asks you, for instance, what you were doing on the 5th of July, your answer should be, "On the 5th of July, I did such and such." So this is simply to focus the debate a little on questions and answers. So, Mr. Petrusic, you have the floor now. I see Mr. Harmon on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I wanted to raise this point before we start the testimony again of General Krstic. Yesterday and the two previous days, we have received a number of exhibits that have English translations attached to them. I noticed in the course of the presentation that there were errors in those English translations in transposing dates and times from the original B/C/S to the English. These are not official translations, and I've been informed by colleagues of mine that there are errors in the text as well. My request, therefore, for the sake of both the Chamber and the sake of the Office of the Prosecutor in preparing cross-examination, is that there -- that these documents that have English, unofficial English translations be submitted to the Language Service Section and that we receive official English language translations before we commence the cross-examination of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, excuse me, but maybe I haven't quite understood. What did you mean by official translations: The translations should be reviewed by the translations service of the Tribunal, or should they be certified in some way?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think they should be reviewed, and if there are errors, they should be corrected, and then an official certified -- not certified in the sense of having a seal, but a Language Service translation should be included in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, this is just as a pure formality, or for some kind of real merit, on the merits, you think. Language can be official or unofficial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Judge Riad, I'm not one that stands on formalities for the sake of standing on formalities. I've been informed by members of my staff that there are errors in the text itself which cause me concern that motivated me to raise this issue with the Chamber. I don't know how many there are; there are apparently a fair number. And I think the Language Service Section, which is available for review of these documents, has at its disposal the draft, the unofficial version, which it can use as a draft, and it shouldn't be too much difficulty for them to review those and prepare a final version of the translation. But I think, for the sake of the record and for the sake of our ability to prepare our cross-examination properly, and the Chamber's ability to consider these documents for the record, there should be clear and accurate translations of the documents that have been tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, we've had at least dozens now of these English translations. I don't know the exact count. Is there realistic expectation that they could be translated in time for your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think, Judge Wald, I think the answer to that question is "Yes." The drafts, the unofficial versions, are comprehensive. The cross-examination, in all likelihood, will not start until next Wednesday, so I do believe, if given those unofficial versions today, we could have official versions to the parties and to the Court by Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic or Mr. Visnjic, have you any comments to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, no particular comments. The only thing I can say is, to give a brief explanation, that from the moment the registry was officially informed, that the registry cannot take upon itself to translate those documents, which was some ten days ago, did everything it could to get those documents translated. The translations were done by several translators, so this may explain differences both in the quality and the use of certain standard terms that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. have become common usage in the Tribunal. So the Defence, too, had certain objections regarding translation, so we quite understand the Prosecution. The only question is, of course, whether the translation and language section can accept the task in time, but that is up to the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Visnjic, as far as I know, I think there are translations which the Defence did themselves, and there are others that were translated here in the Tribunal. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I cannot tell you the exact date, but about two or three weeks ago the Defence offered the registry for the first time a certain number of documents for translation. The language section informed us that they cannot accept that quantity of documents for translation. In fact, I think what I was told was that they could do one document in three days. In the meantime, knowing the schedule and our duty towards the Prosecution to service these documents in time, to serve these documents in time, we took steps to have these documents translated in Belgrade. Some of the documents translated by the language section remain here, and I think Ms. Krystal knows exactly how many documents were translated by the service. Some were translated in Belgrade, and a third group, I'm afraid, remained untranslated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Visnjic, can you identify which documents were translated by yourselves and which were translated by the Tribunal service?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. During the first break we shall inform the registry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Krystal, do you have anything to add on behalf of the registry?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would just like to say that the registry received the Defence's exhibits on October 1st, and it was approximately 275 documents. In translators' terms, it came out to be 300-and-some-odd documents. Obviously, that wasn't possible to translate for an October 16th deadline, so 30 of the hottest documents were chosen to be translated by our section, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the moment, it should be said that the translation service did a very good job. So we have to see which of the documents that were translated here. I think we should not repeat the work, and perhaps we could have the other documents reviewed so as to speed things up a little. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Perhaps I can add some additional clarity to this discussion. Our principal interests are in the documents that are documents of the Republika Srpska. We have less interest, although we would like to see accurate translations of the documents from the army of the -- Bosnian army. Our priority is, first and foremost, to have official translations of all of the VRS documents, if that's of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And how much are they, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Judge Riad, I don't have that number at my disposal. I'll take a look, with the assistance of Ms. Keith, and we can inform the registrar as well during the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you see, given good cooperation, we can come to a solution. So we need to establish contact between the Defence and the registry, who would tell us which documents need reviewing. Also, the Prosecutor can contribute, and Ms. Krystal, with the service, can establish an order of priority for the translations and revisions. Perhaps at the end of the hearing, I don't know whether Ms. Krystal could inform me what is the result of these contacts. For the moment, I think we can continue. Mr. Petrusic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, my learned friends from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Petrusic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we had stopped at the date of the 5th of July in the course of General Krstic's testimony yesterday. So, General, can you briefly tell us what your activities were on the 5th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I did on the 5th of July was the following: Together with the Corps Commander and the other assistant commanders of the corps, we once again made an assessment of the overall situation in the area of responsibility of the corps, particularly in the north-western part of that area and within the area of responsibility of the corps. And we reached the conclusion that it was possible that the forces of the BH army would resume and continue the operation that had been halted and crushed. Also, we came to the conclusion that, in view of the decision of the Corps Commander regarding active combat activities, it was possible to engage the forces which had been detached, for the purpose of active combat action towards Srebrenica, on condition that those activities be completed as soon as possible and that the detached forces be reattached to their original units, according to the decision of the brigade commanders. This went on for several hours, after which I engaged in preparations myself personally for going to the forward command post at Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave for Pribicevac, or rather, when did you arrive at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived at the forward command post at Pribicevac, together with Colonel Vicic, or rather, I left for Pribicevac in the afternoon of the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 5th of July; you left on the 5th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had units envisaged in the order for combat activities around Srebrenica reached their destination?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I left for the forward command post, I had no information that the units had reached the areas where they would -- had been assigned to in combat duty. But going to the Pribicevac command post and passing through Bratunac, I caught up with parts of the Zvornik Brigade who were heading towards Skelani and, from there, on towards the area of deployment as assigned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached the forward command post, did you meet with the commanders of the units participating in the operation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only met with Colonel Blagojevic whose forward command post was in the vicinity of the Pribicevac forward command post of the Drina Corps, and that forward command post was at the Kvac feature. Regarding the other brigade commanders that had been deployed, I did not meet with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what basis did the combat activities begin the next day, the next morning? That's on the 6th of July.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The combat activities of all the units engaged in this operation began on the basis of the order for active combat action that the unit commanders had received as early as on the 4th during the reconnaissance. In that order, there is the item specifying readiness for all the units, and that was 0400 hours on the 6th of July. And that was the only document, and there was no need for any other documents to be issued for the beginning, for the launching of the combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the usher to place Exhibit 77 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document number 08/95, dated July the 6th, 1995. It is addressed from the forward command post of the Drina Corps in Pribicevac and signed by Chief Radislav Krstic. In the English version -- this will probably be one of the documents that Mr. Harmon referred to -- there is no indication of the location. There is no indication that this is the forward command post in Pribicevac, unlike in the original. General, can you please say in this record of yours, which is not signed, is this your report, and what does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise; this is a document of the 6th of July, 1995. I am the signatory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it is typed out, but there is no signature.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an interim combat report that I sent from the forward command post in Pribicevac to the Drina Corps command and the Main Staff of the VRS. The reason why it is an interim report is the fact that combat operations on the 6th of July, 1995, did not, did not go on in the way that we planned and expected. The basic reason was that the forces of the 28th Division on that day offered extremely strong and fierce resistance along all the axes on which our units were engaged. This report, among other things, contains the decision for further activities which is exactly the same as the one issued by the commander in his basic concept. So, it does not diverge from the decision and the concept presented by the Corps Commander in his order for combat action where it is specified that the line that I had shown earlier, Guber Banja-Zivkovo Brdo-Alibegovac feature, Kak feature had to be reached and taken. I can show it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I think we're familiar with the locations, but could you please tell us what, along what -- which axis this resistance came?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially fierce resistance, we encountered it on Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica Bojna-Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask Defence Exhibit 97 to be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is document number -- order number 04/95, dated 6th of July, 1995 issued from the forward command post of the Drina Corps in Pribicevac. This order is not signed either -- or rather, it cannot be seen. You cannot see it here in this text. Can you tell us something about this order, and do you have any knowledge about who issued it?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order that was issued to all the subordinate units from the -- taking part in the operation from the Pribicevac forward command post. I signed it. Immediately after I sent the interim combat report to the commander of the corps and after he received it and studied it, he called me and told me, ordered me, that combat actions should continue in accordance with his decision and his concept, and that, in this sense, I was to issue additional orders, and I did that. And this is precisely the order that I'm talking about. So since on the 6th of July the combat operations did not go on at a pace that we planned and expected, and after I reported to the commander, I issued this order. There is also the decision for the extension of the attack. The attack was to continue on the 7th of July, 1995, and it is stated that all units which had reached a certain lines on the 6th of July, that they should stop where they are, fortify their positions, and set up their support because there was a risk of attack on those units. And then, at dawn on the 7th, they were to continue with their attack and put under their control the line that they were ordered to in the order of the Corps Commander. You can see that this is indeed so from the tasks that I assigned to these units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that this order is in the spirit of the basic order for active combat action?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is fully compliant with the order for active combat action. You can see this from item 2 of the order of the Drina Corps Commander for active combat action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, on the 7th of July, what were you doing on that day, and what were the units in the area doing?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My activities on the 7th of July, very briefly, were the following: Together with Colonel Vicic, we carried out an additional assessment of the situation, and we established the basic reasons why the operation did not go on as envisaged in the decision of the Drina Corps Commander, the basic reasons being that the 28th Division really offered extremely strong and fierce resistance along all the attack axes, in particular on Zeleni Jadar-Bojna-Srebrenica axis. On the 7th of July, the weather conditions were extremely bad in the area, so that the Drina Corps units were, so to speak, virtually unable to carry out any combat activities except for those measures that they were ordered to carry out on the 6th of July. That is what they were to do at the lines that they had reached. There were virtually no combat operations, but the commanders of subordinate units did carry out additional reconnaissance for the purpose of continuing the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 8th of July, where were you and where were the units and the subordinate commanders?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th of July, I was still at the forward command post, and the subordinate commanders were with their units on the axes where the attacks were carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any significant activities?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th of July, the attack continued by all the units that were engaged in the operation, so that, during the day, reports reached us at the forward command post about the activities and successes achieved by the units. On the 9th of July --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, General.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the commander of the Zvornik Brigade reported -- so the commander of the Zvornik Brigade reported at the end of the day that his units, in fact, the 1st Battalion, that was composed of parts of the Zvornik Brigade, that it had managed to place under its control the facility of Tri Sise. That is slightly behind and to the north of Zelini Jadar. The unit commanders, Lieutenant General Andric and Trivic, reported that the 2nd Battalion, composed of their units, managed to place under its control the wider region of Podravanje and Kostur, and that they were continuing their action as ordered in the decision of the Corps Commander towards the Alibegovac and Kak features. The combat group from the Bratunac Brigade did not have any success on that day on the Kvac-Banja Guber axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like Exhibit 78 to be placed on the ELMO. This is a notice of the Drina Corps command. The number is 04/156-5, 8th of July, 1995, signed by commander Major-General Milenko Zivanovic, and it is addressed to the Pribicevac forward command post, attention Chief of Staff, Major General Radislav Krstic, and to the Main Staff of the VRS, attention Major-General Zdravko Tolimir, for his information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please comment on this order, or rather, notice?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document reached me at the forward command post in Pribicevac. This is a document issued by the Main Staff, or rather, General Tolimir, and it was sent to the Drina Corps command. And the Drina Corps commander studied it and forwarded it to me in its original version to the forward command post at Pribicevac. And also it sends the feedback, the return information, to General Tolimir at the Main Staff, informing him that he had studied the document and that the same warning was sent to me at the Pribicevac forward command post. This is in fact a warning to the forces of the Drina Corps engaged in the operation around Srebrenica not to target UNPROFOR forces, because an order had -- or a warning had been received from the UNPROFOR command in Sarajevo by the Main Staff in which it was indicated that such things were happening. At that time, I was not aware of the case. They specify a case in which an UNPROFOR post in Zeleni Jadar area was targeted. At that time, I was not aware of that fact, but I cannot exclude the possibility because of the fact that the 28th Division forces were located in the vicinity, that perhaps a round had gone -- had hit the UN observation post in the Zeleni Jadar area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of the 9th of July, was the composition of the staff officers at the forward command post the same as at the time the forward command post was taken up?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th of July, at the Pribicevac command post, the officers are the same, that is, the officers belonging to the Drina Corps command. However, in the afternoon hours of the same day, General Gvero arrived, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. assistant commander of the Main Staff, for morale, legal, and religious issues. After he had arrived at the forward command post, I briefed him on the situation in the area of active combat action. I was, I must say, surprised by his arrival. He had not been announced and I wasn't expecting General Gvero to arrive at the forward command post. So after I had briefed him about the situation, General Gvero actively joined in the control of the situation. During the course of the combat activities on that day, he made certain suggestions and he proposed the kind of measures that were to be taken so that the active combat operations would be conducted in the way that was envisaged. I realised that General Gvero was not happy with the rhythm of the attack of the Drina Corps units, and I also realised that the Main Staff had had information about that earlier on and that he actually came there to follow the situation on the ground and probably to inform General Mladic thereof. He didn't take command in any way over the units of the corps which were engaged for the purposes of that operation. He was merely doing what I have just described.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you mean that he made suggestions, certain recommendations, and that he consulted you, advised you, and that he in no way issued orders or took command over the units?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. He didn't take command; he didn't issue orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to have the Exhibit 79 placed on the ELMO, please. This is a document which was issued by the General Staff of the VRS on the 9th of July, 1995. The document bears number 19/46-501. The document was issued by Major-General Zdravko Tolimir. This document was addressed to -- was forwarded to the president of Republika Srpska and also it was addressed to the forward command post for the attention of Generals Gvero and Krstic and also to the Drina Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you give us your view and your interpretation of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document confirms what I have just said, that on the 9th of July, General Gvero arrived at the Pribicevac forward command post. It can be seen from the document that both myself and General Gvero were the addressees of the document, but that the document was also forwarded to the president of Republika Srpska. Obviously, the general staff of the VRS had received from the Drina Corps command certain information and reports, and it's also clear that they were following the situation and informing the general command of the army of Republika Srpska about the situation. In this document, one can also see that the president of Republika Srpska is ordering that combat activities be continued, and that members of UNPROFOR be protected as well as the Muslim civilian population in the area of Srebrenica, and that safety should be guaranteed to them if they crossed to the territory of Republika Srpska. I don't think I should comment on this particular bit, if they crossed to the territory of Republika Srpska. I think that they're probably referring to UNPROFOR forces here. In this order, one can see that the president of Republika Srpska is also ordering that combat activities be continued towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record and for the Chamber and my learned colleagues, I should like to say that this document is identical to the Prosecution document 432 as regards its contents; however, these two exhibits differ as to the manner in which they were typed and processed, so they probably come from two different sources. This is just for your information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I should like to move on to the 10th of July at this point.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, perhaps -- you said, "Protect the Muslim population if they cross to Republika Srpska." If they crossed or if they crossed to -- are they going to Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are you addressing the question to me, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If they crossed to the territory. Is it just the passage, or --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they're referring to the members of UNPROFOR here in this portion of the text: If they cross over to the territory of Republika Srpska, if they cross over to the army of Republika Srpska for the purposes of their protection. No, not the Muslim population because President Karadzic is saying here how the civilian population should be treated inside the protected area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have exhibit number 432 placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 432, let us try to clarify and to avoid any misunderstandings. I'm referring to paragraph 3 of this document. Would you read it out for us, General?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 3 of this document, the president of Republika Srpska ordered that combat operations be continued and that full protection be ensured to UNPROFOR members and the Muslim population, and that they be guaranteed safety in the event of their crossover to the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you intend to stick to the timetable that we adopted, I should like to suggest a break at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we will have a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go back briefly to these two exhibits, OTP 432 and D79, please. Please tell us when they were received at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The content of this document is the same as that of the previous document, and it was received at 2350 hours on the 9th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we are talking about the document P432, and the document that has been marked as 79?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could you please provide the witness with document 79.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This second document was received at 23 -- I'm afraid I can't read the rest. It's illegible. It looks as if it's 2300 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we go on to the 10th of July, tell us, please: On the 9th of July, in addition to these reports that arrived at the forward command post, were there any other activities of any significance going on?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to receiving these reports at the forward command post of Pribicevac, reports were also coming in from subordinate units about the progress in combat operations, so that the commander of the 1st Battalion, which belonged to the Zvornik Brigade, reported -- this was a report in the evening -- that his units had gained control of Zivkovo Brdo feature and reached the line of deployment assigned to him in the order for active combat action by the Corps Commander. However, another report came from the same commander, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, that forces of the 28th Division, during the night, sometime around midnight, had staged a counteroffensive and pushed back his forces from this feature. A report came from the command of the 2nd Battalion, that is, from the forces of the 1st Bircani Brigade and the 2nd Romanija Brigade, which compiled this battalion, that their battalion had continued combat action and was engaged in battle to gain control of the Alibegovac feature and the feature Kak. The command of the Bratunac Brigade reported from his forward command post at Kvac that on that day no significant progress had been made towards Divljakinje and the Kupusna -- Banja.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Banja Guber. The interpreter corrects herself. Banja Guber.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in the afternoon, in the late afternoon, about 1700 hours, at the Pribicevac forward command post, without any prior announcement, without me being informed about it, General Mladic, the commander of the Main Staff, arrived, together with the commander of the Drina Corps, General Zivanovic. Of course, I reported to the Superior Commanders and briefed them on the situation and the problems we had encountered up to then in implementing the idea, or rather, the decision of the Corps Commander on active combat action. They continued to monitor combat operations because the Drina Corps units had still not reached the line assigned to them, Divljakinje, Banja Guber, Zivkovo Brdo, Alibegovac, and the Kak feature. They did not interfere very much regarding the actual conduct of operations, they just monitored them. I said that this was a surprise for me, I mean their coming to the forward command post, because General Gvero was there, and then General Mladic, the commander of the Main Staff, arrived. So my conclusion was that they were obviously dissatisfied with the course the combat actions were taking. I also gathered after their arrival that General Gvero had in fact come to control and check the Pribicevac forward command post, to monitor operations, and to report the commander of the Main Staff about the same, so he probably did do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, did all the senior officers you have just mentioned, General Gvero, Mladic, and Zivanovic, did they all attend; and what was happening in the surroundings?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, 1995, at the Pribicevac forward command post, all the senior officers who had been at the forward command post remained, and that is myself, Colonel Vicic, Lieutenant Colonel Osoric, Major Jeldjevic, and Lieutenant Amovic. General Gvero was no longer there. General Mladic and General Zivanovic were also there. Immediately after coming, they joined in observing and monitoring the combat operations, and after the unit commanders had sent their reports, the commander of the 1st Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade reporting that he had regained control of Zivkovo Brdo in the early hours of the morning, whereby he reported that he had accomplished his task. The commander of the 2nd Battalion, Colonel Andric, and as I have already said, that battalion consisted of the forces of the 1st Bircani Brigade and the 2nd Romanija Brigade, so Colonel Andric and Colonel Trivic were there. He is the commander of the 2nd Romanija Brigade. And Colonel Andric reported that they had reached the line formed by Alibegovac and Kak, and that they had gained control of those points, and thereby accomplished their task. Then the command of the Bratunac Brigade reports that he's having a great deal of problems with his soldiers to persuade them to embark upon their task of gaining control of Banja Guber and Divljakinje. After the commanders of the units had submitted their reports and accomplished their tasks, then General Mladic, via a radio transmitter, RUP 12, which was encrypted, called up each of those commanders who had reported that they had accomplished the task, and he introduced himself by saying, "This is Panorama 01. You haven't accomplished your task. Continue the attack. Enter Srebrenica." He said literally, "I am now in command of the forces engaged in this operation." After this order, the commanders of subordinate units did indeed undertake to accomplish their task. Sometime in the evening of the 10th, early evening, the commander of the 1st Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade reported that he had gained control of the Bojna feature on the route Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica -- Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica, and that a part of the forces were still at Zivkovo Brdo. The commander of the 2nd Battalion reported that he had captured the feature Siljato Brdo. So they continued their attack, the 2nd Battalion continued its attack from the Alibegovac and Kak features, and they gained control of the Siljato Brdo feature. This was in the early evening. It is already dusk, and these units stopped at the lines that they had reached and temporarily assumed the defensive position for -- because it was dark and they were not in contact with the forces of the 28th Division. I would just like to note that after continuing their attack from their previous lines to the Bojna -- towards the Bojna feature and towards the Siljato Brdo feature, there was no significant resistance on the part of the 28th Division. There was just some sporadic fire. When they reached the Bojna-Siljato Brdo line in the evening, the units temporarily took up their defence. And the Bratunac Brigade forces again had virtually no success at all. They had gained control only of a part of the Divljakinje feature. I would like to add the following: General Mladic really did take direct control over -- command over the brigade commanders and issued orders to them, to all of them. And I realised that he did not have the role of a controller, that he was not there to monitor the combat operations and to give guidelines to the units, or suggestions, but that it was for him to have the role of a commander in the continuation of the attack towards Srebrenica for the purpose of actually entering the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was General Zivanovic after that? Do you have an active role in the command?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After General Mladic assumed the command or the role of the commander, General Zivanovic and myself no longer had this role. We were merely following the orders of the chief of Main Staff and the way in which the units were implementing these orders. Those who knew General Mladic from previous events and cases, it was known that he very often took over in certain parts of the front in Bosnia-Herzegovina of -- he took upon himself the role of the battalion commander, or a company leader even in some cases. He told us, "You see now, this is the way to exert command."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 11th of July, 1995, were there any combat operations going on? Where were you, General Zivanovic, General Mladic? Was General Gvero still there? Did he leave? Can you tell us something briefly about that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Gvero had left the Pribicevac forward command post in the afternoon of the 9th of July. I have already said that. At the Pribicevac forward command post, in addition to the group that we already know of that was there from before, Generals Mladic and Zivanovic were present there too. On the 11th of July, at dawn, the units engaged in this operation continued their attack in order to carry out the orders received by General Mladic. He was in continual contact with them and he issued his commands to them over a Motorola. On all the attack axes, and I'm referring now primarily to the 1st and 2nd Battalions, there was virtually no resistance by the 28th Division except again ahead of the front where the first Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade attacked towards the Divljakinje feature and in the location of Guber Banja. These were the only features. They are very close to Srebrenica, and that is the reason why there was still resistance that was slightly stronger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were reserve forces committed to battle on this axis?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade reported directly to General Mladic that he was encountering problems with his personnel that was assigned to carry out the attack and that they simply were unable or did not want to go ahead, and some of them had in fact fled, General Mladic ordered that, on this axis, an attack should be launched at any cost, and he orders General Zivanovic to provide Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. additional forces from the Drina Corps for their engagement along this axis. This was in the morning of the 11th of July, 1995. General Zivanovic called the commander of the 1st Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade and ordered him to bring a unit, about 50- to 60-men strong -- that would be a smaller company -- to the Kvac area of the forward command post of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. The commander of the 1st Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade detached the required number of personnel and, with the company commander, sent this unit to the Kvac area that I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These units that obviously continued with their attacks and the actual entry into the town of Srebrenica, you said that they did not encounter any significant resistance. So they enter Srebrenica. What happened in that interval between the morning hours and the entry into the town itself?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the Drina Corps units, in my opinion, I would say, were on the surrounding heights from the east -- to the east and south of Srebrenica, the heights that are close to the city and around it, in the afternoon, I think it was sometime between 1300 and 1400 hours, the aviation started to target our positions, primarily in the Kvac feature, Pribicevac feature, and Bojna feature. This attack, if I remember correctly, lasted for about 30 minutes. And in light of the previous overflights of the airplanes which did not fire, and after they did open fire on the features that I have just mentioned. When the airstrikes stopped, General Mladic ordered the unit commanders to take all measures to air defence, to defend themselves from attacks from the air space. I will give you an example. For instance, the burning of haystacks in order to create smokescreens, this is one of the measures, one of the air defence measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, you were at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was at Pribicevac. General Zivanovic, the Corps Commander, and General Mladic was there, and the rest of the group that I have mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you get information that the units have entered the town?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in the afternoon, I think it was around 1700 hours, the commander of the 1st Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, reported to the chief of Main Staff that he had entered the town, that part of his units had entered the town, and the other commanders reported that their units are on the heights around the town, in the vicinity of the town, very close to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, not all of the units entered the town.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic reported to the chief of Main Staff that a part of his unit had entered the town, then General Mladic commanded me and General Zivanovic to follow him to Srebrenica, to come with him to Srebrenica. Of course, we immediately set off in our respective vehicles along the Pribicevac-Zeleni Jadar-Bojna-Srebrenica route. As we entered Srebrenica, we encountered Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, who reported to the chief of Main Staff, saying that a part of his unit, around a hundred soldiers, had entered the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you find in the very centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the centre of the town, in addition to Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, who had already entered the town, we met with Colonel Trivic, commander of the 2nd Motorised Brigade, Colonel Andric, and several other officers from their units. Colonel Trivic, on that occasion, reported to the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the centre of the town, there's you, General Zivanovic, General Mladic, and a report is being made to General Mladic. Was that a regular thing to do in terms of ranks? Was it a customary thing, to report to the highest-ranking officer?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a common military rule.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you entered the town, in addition to the officers that you have mentioned, did you also see Lieutenant Colonel Popovic and Lieutenant Pelemis who was the commander of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of this operation, throughout that period of time, did Lieutenant Colonel Popovic -- was Lieutenant Colonel Popovic present in any way, either on a regular basis or from time to time, at the Pribicevac forward command post?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Lieutenant Colonel Popovic did not at any point in time show up at the Pribicevac forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you entered Srebrenica, did you see members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica, I did see soldiers, but I don't know what unit they belonged to, the soldiers who were in Srebrenica. I thought that they were the soldiers of the Drina Corps units. So I didn't notice, nor did I pay any attention to, the unit from which those soldiers may have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment have a typical uniform, if one can call it that way. It is a black uniform, and I should like to know whether you could observe, whether you indeed noticed that black uniform which would enable you to identify them as members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Due to the length of time that I spent at my post as the Chief of Staff of the corps, I was not in a position, I was not in a situation to know all of the officers at the corps, so I didn't know all of the battalion commanders in subordinate units, let alone know the soldiers from some other unit which was not part of the organisational structure of the Drina Corps. The fact that they were wearing black uniforms, I wasn't paying any attention to that. In those times, various uniforms were being worn. We had soldiers who wore uniforms which resembled the uniforms worn by NATO soldiers. We even have uniforms which were similar to the uniforms of the BiH army soldiers. I simply didn't pay any attention to them, and the fact that I passed by didn't enable me to notice anything in particular. It didn't strike me as anything strange. I didn't even think about that. I didn't think about what unit they may have been members of and what soldiers they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the forward command post, did you at any point in time receive any piece of information to the effect that that particular unit might show up in Srebrenica and take part in the operations around and in Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Neither myself nor any of my staff officers, I'm referring to the group who came with me to the forward command post, we didn't have any knowledge, any information to the effect that the 10th Sabotage Detachment had arrived in the area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Trivic reported to General Mladic. What happened next amongst the officers who were there?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Colonel Trivic had made a report to the commander of the Main Staff and after we had greeted the present officers, the commander of the Main Staff ordered the brigade commanders to continue immediately with the attack in the direction of Potocari and Bratunac. After he had issued such an order, we were confused, and we realised that his decision, his order, was not a logical one. It made no sense, simply because, through our intelligence data, we knew that the civilian population from the surrounding villages of the town of Srebrenica, in particular to the south of Srebrenica, on the previous days and on that very day, had already set out in the direction of Potocari, towards the UN base. This is what the brigade commanders said to the commander of the Main Staff, and they explained to him that, should the units continue with the attack towards Potocari and Bratunac, there would be extremely severe consequences for the VRS and also for the civilian population which was already in Potocari. At the time, we still didn't know and we still didn't have contact with the 28th Division. We didn't know whether they had managed to pull out. We didn't know whether the members of the 28th Division were perhaps at the UN base, around the UN base together with the civilian population. And if we should continue with the attack, we thought that the consequences would indeed be severe. I say consequences for both sides because the soldiers who were engaged in the operation were euphoric, and that euphoria was encouraged, and one could see it on that videotape by the behaviour of General Zivanovic, because of his orders and his behaviour in general. So after the brigade commanders explained this to the commander of the Main Staff, General Mladic ordered that the troops should stop at the lines they had taken control of. I have already stated it, only about a hundred soldiers had entered the town; however, the main body of the forces from the south and the east side of Srebrenica had remained on the surrounding heights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that General Zivanovic had issued an order and that there was a danger because of the euphoric state of mind that the soldiers were in. What General Zivanovic are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I said General Mladic and not General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have probably misspoken, General. You were talking about the activities of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to the order which was issued by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This order concerns both you and General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It concerns myself and General Zivanovic. After the brigade commanders had received the order to hold the attack on the lines that had been reached and to stabilise the deployment of the units, they indeed did Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. so, and they went back to their units. But General Mladic then ordered that General Zivanovic and myself, the brigade commanders, and Major Jevdjevic report to him at a meeting that was supposed to take place at the Bratunac Brigade command in Bratunac on that same evening at 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you left Srebrenica and went to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't leave Srebrenica for Bratunac. Immediately after we had received the order and had been informed about the meeting -- the time of the meeting and my presence there, I went back to the Pribicevac forward command post along the Srebrenica-Bojna-Zeleni Jadar-Pribicevac axis. So, I went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you find at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Pribicevac forward command post, I found Colonel Vicic, Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric, and the commander of the staff command, Lieutenant Amovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those were probably already evening hours?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was already evening, around 8.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, at that point, leave Pribicevac and go to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had briefed Colonel Vicic about what General Mladic had ordered, that is, that the units should stop at the lines and stabilise their positions, I ordered Colonel Vicic to continue monitoring the situation in the units. And after that, I left for Bratunac along the Pribicevac-Sase-Bratunac route. So I left along this route, Pribicevac-Sase-Voljevica-Bratunac, and I arrived in the Bratunac Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can conclude that you did not take the route which goes through Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this route didn't go through Potocari. This was the route that we had used prior to the beginning of the operation in order to reach the forward command post at Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point, Mr. President, I should like to suggest a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us have a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Briefly, General, talking about the 11th of July, when the NATO forces were operating, were there any casualties among members of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the NATO air force shelled Caus, Pribicevac, and the Bojna feature, after they bombed these features, the forces of the Drina Corps, in terms of personnel, did not suffer any casualties. There was only a large number of soldiers who suffered contusions -- concussions because of the explosions, and there was damage on motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have Exhibit 80, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you reached the forward command post at Pribicevac from Srebrenica. You issued certain assignments to Colonel Vicic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit number 80 bears the number 03/4-1617, dated the 11th of July, 1995. It is issued by the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, by assistant commander Major-General Milan Gvero to the Drina Corps command at the forward command post number 1. Were you familiar with the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I went back to the forward command post at Pribicevac from Srebrenica, I was given this document and I was familiar with its content. It is directly addressed to the Drina Corps command at the forward command post number 1 of the Drina Corps at Pribicevac. Just as I was familiar with the previous warning with respect to UNPROFOR, so I also studied this document sent by the assistant commander for morale, legal, and religious issues, General Milan Gvero. I do not recollect what day it was prior to this date when the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Colonel Vinko Pandurevic, informed me that forces, or rather soldiers of the Dutch Battalion who were at a checkpoint near Zeleni Jadar had surrendered, or rather had crossed to the forces of Republika Srpska, the reason being that they were afraid of retaliation by troops of the BH army and of the 28th Division and that they might be used against the forces of the VRS and that they simply would be having trouble with them. I was also informed by the commander of the Zvornik Brigade that this group of soldiers was sent to Bratunac. I don't remember what day that was. It could have been sometime between the end of the day of the 8th of July and the 10th of July, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you arrived from Pribicevac to Bratunac, to the already scheduled meeting. This is the evening by now, so could you explain what was happening that evening and where the meeting was held.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, as I have already said, ordered General Zivanovic, myself, Major Jevdjevic, and the brigade commanders engaged in this operation to report to him at a meeting of the command of the Bratunac Brigade at 2200 hours. When I arrived to the command of the Bratunac Brigade, in the hall where the meeting was due to be held, I found the following officers: the commander of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic; the commander of the 1st Birac Infantry Brigade, Colonel Andric; the commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, Colonel Blagojevic; the commander of the Milici Brigade, Major Nastic. Also present when I arrived was Major Jevdjevic, who was not at the forward command post Pribicevac when I returned there from Srebrenica. After some time, around 2000 hours -- no, I'm sorry, about 2200 hours -- not later, it may have been a couple of minutes earlier than that -- General Mladic arrived at the brigade headquarters, together with General Zivanovic, when the meeting actually began.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the commanding officers you have listed, were officers from the Security Service also present at any level whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a single officer of any level from the Security Service was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the intelligence service?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the meeting began, and who chaired the meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting started, and it was chaired by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, what was the topic of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing he told us was that he and General Zivanovic had just returned from a meeting with a commander of the Dutch UNPROFOR Battalion, Colonel Karremans. He did not provide any details regarding the substance of that meeting; he just told us that it had been held. After that, he ordered that the forces of the Drina Corps which had participated in the operation Krivaja 95 until Srebrenica was entered, should, during the night, be pulled out and gather in the area of Viogora, in the area of Viogora to the west of Srebrenica, as indicated by these arrows. This is the area he meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for the record, it should be noted that it is the area of the mountain of Viogora which is to the northwest of Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: West of Srebrenica, west of Srebrenica. And after that, that they should organise a march and head for -- along the following route: Viogora, Suceska, Derventa, Milici, Vlasenica, Han Pijesak, Plane, and that they should prepare for offensive operations for Zepa. In that connection, he also said the following: He ordered, saying, "General Krstic will be the commander of these forces that will be conducting the operation for Zepa."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or any of the others present comment on the decision or order issued by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately after this order was issued, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, said the following: "General, sir, we still have no contact with the 28th Division. We don't know where it is situated. Possibly the 28th Division will make a breakthrough towards the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade which would have unforeseeable consequences for that brigade." General Mladic immediately responded to this comment by Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic addressed to him and said, "Lieutenant Colonel, your task is Zepa. The area of Bratunac and Srebrenica have been reached by forces of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, a unit of the Main Staff, a police detachment of a special MUP Brigade, and also there's the 65th Protective Motorised Regiment in the area of Nova Kasaba."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any further questions or comments?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said, "I will be in command of these and other forces in this area, and you will go where I have ordered you to go." Also, General Mladic, as soon as he had issued his order for the forces of the Drina Corps to pull out and congregate in the area of Viogora mountain, he ordered Jevdjevic to go to the next forward command post. Major Jevdjevic immediately left the meeting and went to carry out his assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, can we have exhibit number D98.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the order number 03/4-1616, dated the 11th of July, 1995. It is issued by the commander Lieutenant General Ratko Mladic. It is designated as very urgent and it is addressed to the command of the Drina Corps, the 65th Protective Motorised Regiment, the 67th Communications Regiment, and for the information of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, the 1st Vlasenica, the 1st Milici, and the 1st Podrinje Brigades. General, could you please comment on this order.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen this order before. In fact, I did study it so that I can give you a comment. This is an order to the Drina Corps command, to the 65th Protective Motorised Regiment, and the 67th Communications Regiment -- this was also a unit of the Main Staff -- and for the information of the Drina Corps units. That's the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade; the 1st Vlasenica Brigade, Infantry, Light Brigade; the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade; and the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade. It refers to the information related to the request of the 28th Division, of the command of the 28th Division, for the forces of the 28th Division that had been transferred from Srebrenica and Zepa, as planned, to the Sarajevo theatre, for them to immediately head to Srebrenica, or return to Srebrenica. This order also provides the axes along which they are to return, and these are the shortest routes leading to Srebrenica and Zepa, and I will mention them. The first axis was Medov Do -- I will show it later -- Sljemenska Planina, Devetak, Boksanica Mountain, Zepa, Srebrenica. This is the wider area of the municipality of Olovo, Medov Do, then -- I'm showing it on the map now -- Sljemenska Planina, Devetak -- it is not on the map -- the Boksanica Mountain -- it is not on the map -- Zepa, and on to Srebrenica. The second axis was Spiljanska Stijena, Igrista, Partizansko Polje, Zezenica, Kupusna, and on through Stedra and Nurici, towards Kosovo and Srebrenica. This is the axis here: Spiljanska Stijena, Tamburica Kosa, Han Pogled, Zezenica, Nurici, Podravanje, Srebrenica. So we're talking about the transfer of the forces of the 28th Division, which had, according to the plan, been pulled out from Srebrenica and Zepa to the Sarajevo theatre in order to take part in the spring offensive. This indicates that they had assembled in the area of Olovo and Kladanj and that they were to return from these axes to Srebrenica and to Zepa. This order also gives a task to the units of the Drina Corps, such as the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, which was manning these positions facing Olovo and Kladanj; and to the Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade, which was also engaged on the front towards Kladanj; and to the 1st Podrinje Infantry Brigade, which was engaged between Zepa and Rogatica on positions facing Zepa; and to the 65th Protective Motorised Regiment, which was engaged from the direction of Han Pijesak, towards Zepa, in the defence. So through the areas of responsibility of these units, the forces of the 28th Division were supposed to pass. This order also shows, in a very obvious way, that the commander of the Main Staff assigns separate tasks to the Drina Corps and separately to the 65th Protective Motorised Regiment and to the 67th Communications Regiment. As regards the tasks issued to the 65th Protective Regiment, the commander reminds them that they will be carrying out this task parallel to the task that they had received earlier. That is all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that this task had already been given to the 65th Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Regiment, or is it some other task that it had been given earlier?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order specifies that this is a task that the regiment had received earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you received this order at that meeting, and did the meeting end with this order?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The meeting did not end as yet --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The witness testified that he had never seen this order before and the question says -- that was asked by my colleague was, "So you received this order at the meeting," which appears to be a conflict between the two, and we would object to the leading question. And if there is a clarification that needs to be made, perhaps it should be made by General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when I was asking my last question to which Mr. Harmon objected, I was referring to the order that General Mladic issued at the meeting on the 11th of July in the evening at 2200 hours, and the order referred to the operation that was supposed to be taken towards Zepa, and I was not referring to the order that General Krstic has been commenting on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Petrusic, but you should try and ask your questions as clearly as possible in order to avoid any confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, after General Mladic in the evening hours of the 11th had issued assignments regarding Zepa, did the meeting end?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The meeting went on for a little while, and during that time, General Mladic informed all those who were present at the meeting of the fact that he had received a decree from the president of Republika Srpska to the effect that the civilian commissioner in Srebrenica should be appointed, and that Mr. Deronjic should be appointed commissioner, and that he was supposed to establish a civilian authority in the town itself and in the territory of the Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you as Chief of Staff at that meeting, you and other officers who were present at the meeting, did you know anything about the 28th Division and the route via which it was leaving the enclave?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even before this meeting, immediately after we had entered the town and also during the meeting at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, we didn't know anything, we didn't have any knowledge about the forces of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your activities after the meeting ended? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting, General Mladic ordered me to come to a meeting that was supposed to be held at 2300 hours at the Fontana Hotel in Bratunac. After he had ordered me that, he left the headquarters, together with General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That order, or rather, notice about a meeting, was it received by any other officer who was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. None of the officers who were present at the meeting received this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That meeting was supposed to start at 11 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The meeting began at 2300 hours on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the participants of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting at the Fontana Hotel in Bratunac which started at 2300 on the 11th of July was attended by General Mladic, myself, then there was a colonel whom we hadn't seen from before but later on. During the proceedings in this case, mention was made of Colonel Jankovic, and that was him. Present at the meeting was also the chief of security of the Drina Corps, Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, and my assistant commander for intelligence affairs, Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric. There were several other individuals from the civilian authorities, and I believe that the meeting was also attended by the president of the municipal assembly of Bratunac, Mr. Simic. Colonel Karremans, the commander of the Dutch Battalion, also attended the meeting, together with one or two other of his officers, his subordinates. Present at the meeting was also the representatives of Bosniaks, Mr. Mandzic, whom I didn't know, whom I hadn't met before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was General Zivanovic present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, General Zivanovic was not present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether General Zivanovic, the Corps Commander, and we are talking about the 11th of July, was he the commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the Corps Commander, and the reason why he was absent was probably because he was involved in some other matters according to his own plan or pursuant to orders of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we are still in the field of hypothesis, his involvement, could it have been in the drafting of the orders for combat activities which were to take place in the area of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, please, would you ask your witness for specific information and do not engage in speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, at that time while this meeting was being held, do you know whether anyone was involved in the preparations of everything that should accompany an operation such as the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that moment, I -- all I could do was to think about the manner in which the Drina Corps forces could be taken to Zepa and used further on. That was my job. That was my responsibility. I was the only one who could do that because General Mladic had issued a clear order to the -- that I was to be the commander for those operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go back to the meeting. What was on the agenda?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The subject of the meeting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, I'm sorry to interrupt you, I don't know if I am right, but it seems to me that General Krstic would need a break at this point. I don't know whether -- it seems to me that he's in pain. I might be wrong. Am I right or wrong, General?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, you are right. I would need a break at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. We will have a break now, quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 12.32 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, we had stopped at the meeting of the 11th, at 2300 hours. Could you tell us, what was the agenda of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very hard for me to remember the exact contents of the whole meeting, but I will tell you what I do remember. General Mladic, with the representative of the Bosniak side, Mr. Mandzic, was having a dialogue. Of course, he spoke much more than did Mr. Mandzic. He was saying to Mr. Mandzic that the Muslims in the area, from the very beginning of the conflict to that day, had committed great atrocities against the Serb population and that is why the army of Republika Srpska had been forced to carry out such an operation. He also said that he had nothing against the civilian population, that the aim of the Republika Srpska and its army was not the civilian population, but he wanted him to give him information as to the location of the 28th Division, where they had gone to. He also told him that all those who had committed crimes from among the members of that division must be held to account for what they had done. He requested that he get in touch with the 28th Division and that he should advise them to surrender their weapons, to lay down their arms and to surrender, and that it is quite normal that measures would be taken against those for which there is available information that they -- and evidence that they had committed war crimes. And he guaranteed that all those who surrender would be safe and that nothing would happen to any one of them. Upon this address by General Mladic to Mr. Mandzic, Mr. Mandzic responded very briefly. He mostly listened to General Mladic and told him that he didn't know where the 28th Division was and that even if he did know, if he were to convey General Mladic's demand on surrender and the laying down of weapons, they wouldn't listen to him and they would not comply to such a request. He also told him that the civilian population, which was just then in the UNPROFOR base, the base of the Dutch Battalion in Potocari, could stay if they wished to, could stay in Srebrenica, to live there; or, according to their own wishes, they might decide to go to the territory under the control of the BH army. He requested that he contact the people and communicate this to them. Mr. Mandzic said then, I think, that he had no special influence, as he had said in respect of the 28th Division that he had no particular influence over the people to be able to influence their decision. Mr. Mandzic said a number of times that they were not in touch with the presidency in Sarajevo, because regarding the decision as to whether to stay or to go to territory under their control, they would need to contact them. General Mladic did not respond to this. Mr. Mandzic also said that there were very serious problems in Potocari, that there was a very large group of people there, that they were mostly without food, and that they were even in short supply of water. General Mladic said that he would take care of providing the population with food and water, of course with the assistance of the Dutch Battalion, of the UNPROFOR. He also spoke to the commander of the Dutch Battalion, Colonel Karremans, in connection with the laying down of weapons and the surrender of the 28th Division. One could say that this was a kind of ultimatum, that he had to contact them and convey to them his request. Also, he requested from Colonel Karremans that, should the population decide to abandon the territory of Srebrenica, or rather, the UN compound, that the Dutch Battalion must help them to a certain degree to address all problems, and especially those related to fuel supplies, petrol, which would be necessary if motor vehicles were to be used. The meeting did not last long, and General Mladic was talking most of the time; the others were silent. All the other representatives of the Serb side were silent. He was the only one to speak, with occasional responses to demands by General Mladic being given by the commander of the Dutch Battalion and by Mr. Mandzic. The meeting ended I think about, as far as I can recollect, 2400 hours without any kind of decision having been made at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and the others attending the meeting did not take the floor?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one except General Mladic took the floor about anything at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that meeting, did you have any contact or conversation with General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no contact, but he only told all those present that there would be another meeting the next day, on the 12th of July, beginning at 1000 hours. He didn't tell me at all that I needed to attend the meeting of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go after that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the meeting ended, I went to the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade, to sleep there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next day, the 12th of July, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My activities were primarily linked with the tasks assigned to me in connection with the Zepa operation. I got up early, at 6.00. I dropped in to see the duty officer, and he told me that General Mladic had ordered that I should attend again the meeting at 1000 hours. After that, I immediately went to the forward command post at Pribicevac, where I found Colonel Vicic and the commander of the staff command, Lieutenant Amovic, at the forward command post Pribicevac. I went to Pribicevac from Bratunac, taking the same route I had taken to go to the meeting, and that is Bratunac, Voljevica, Sase, Pribicevac.
