When I reached the Pribicevac forward command post, I conveyed to Colonel Vicic immediately the tasks we had been assigned linked to Zepa, and I told him that, in that connection, we had very, very little time because the units had to be congregated, led to the deployment lines, and that we needed to prepare the most fundamental documents linked to that operation. On the spot, we discussed this assignment. I gave Colonel Vicic the basic guidelines as to what he had to do while he was still at the Pribicevac forward command post in that connection, and I passed on to him certain points regarding the drafting of the order and the specification of tasks for subordinate units. When I reached the Pribicevac forward command post and having completed these activities, I went back to the meeting I had been ordered to attend at the Fontana Hotel in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That meeting was attended by the same persons, almost by the same persons who had attended the previous meeting, except for one additional representative of Bosniaks, a lady that was there as well. As for the Serb side, the participants were mostly the same as those present at the previous meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Muslim side was represented by Mr. Mandzic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mandzic and this lady whose name escapes me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As regards officers of the Drina Corps or the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Main Staff, present was General Mladic, Colonel Jankovic. I can't remember whether anyone else was present. As for the Drina Corps, I myself was there, Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, and Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric. Yes, I remember. There was one other officer from the Main Staff, Lieutenant Colonel Milutinovic, who was chief of intelligence service at the -- information service at the information, morale, and religious department, religious issues department. The meeting was also attended by the president of the Bratunac Municipal Assembly and the newly-appointed commissioner for Srebrenica, Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Dutch Battalion? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Dutch Battalion was represented by Colonel Karremans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about the agenda of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agenda was more or less the same as during the first meeting, and again General Mladic spoke at some length, or rather talked to the representatives of the Bosniak community, especially with the lady who attended the meeting. He requested that Mr. Mandzic and the lady, that they should tell him what the residents of Srebrenica, or rather the protected area of Srebrenica, had decided. As far as I remember, the lady said that they had decided that they would go to the free territory. General Mladic said the same he did at the previous meeting. He told Mr. Mandzic that they could decide to remain in the territory of Republika Srpska or to leave for the free territory. I think that she said that they had decided that they would go to Tuzla and Kladanj. The lady engaged in a conversation for some time with the people whom she knew. I believe she talked to Mr. Deronjic, but I cannot remember the details of their conversation. And as far as Colonel Karremans is concerned, he told him the same thing as at the previous meeting; he requested fuel again and the surrender of the 28th Division. But I can't remember what Colonel Karremans told him about the fuel, but as far as the 28th Division is concerned, he said he was unable to meet his request because it was simply impossible. He also said that should the population be moved, or rather evacuated, that in that case, as far as the escort is concerned, the UNPROFOR forces should also take part in that. At that time, it was already obvious that the evacuation would take place very soon, on the basis of all the questions that General Mladic asked and the comments that were made in relation to that, and also because of what the lady said, that they had decided, that is, that they would go to the territory under the control of the BH government. During this meeting, at least as far as the military personnel is concerned -- I'm referring to the Serb side -- nobody said anything. Nobody took the floor or engaged in any discussion. It was General Mladic who spoke all the time. As for the civilians, I already told you that Mr. Deronjic spoke with the lady who was representing the Bosniak community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the meeting had ended, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting, which I believe ended around 1200 hours on that day, I went back to the Pribicevac forward command post. My intention was to pass through Srebrenica on that occasion, but I ran into a checkpoint at Potocari which was manned by the troops of the 65th Protective Motorised Regiment, and the soldiers there told me that nobody could pass through the checkpoint before General Mladic and that that was his order, and indeed this is how I interpreted that: as an order. So I respected it, because the soldiers are supposed to respect orders issued by their superiors. And also I thought -- I didn't have anyone with me as my escort except for my driver, and I actually didn't know what was happening with the refugees up there, so I respected the request that was made by the soldiers manning the checkpoint. While I was there for this very brief period of time, I listened to those soldiers, but at the same time I noticed the presence of a TV crew there. They asked me to get out of my vehicle, and I gave them a brief interview, and it was indeed a very brief interview. The moment I got out of the vehicle, I realised that Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric was there as well, together with Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, and I ordered Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric to report to me at the forward command post on the 13th in the morning. I didn't order anything to Lieutenant Colonel Popovic because I was not his subordinate officer. He was an assistant commander of the corps, like myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you order to Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric is my -- I'm superior officer to him. He was the assistant commander for intelligence section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the interview -- actually, tell us about the contents of the interview, first of all.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The topic of the interview concerned the task that we were accomplishing. They wanted to know what I thought about NATO air strikes, and I gave my opinion. They asked me about the civilians, and I told them that a meeting had just been completed and that it had been agreed that they would be transferred to the free territory, and also that safety and security was guaranteed during the evacuation through their representatives who attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and my apologies for the interruption. I'm not sure if this is a mistake or not, but on line 12:56:08 is a reference, "Colonel Popovic because I was not his subordinate officer." I'm not sure if that is an error or if that's the way the record should stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously the record is not correct. Let us try and clarify it through a question. Thank you, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, is he your subordinate?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he was not my subordinate officer and that I was not his superior officer. He was an assistant commander to the Corps Commander with the same level as myself, who was the Chief of Staff; and he had the same authority as myself when -- in terms of relationship with the commanders from his section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you saw those officers at the checkpoint, Kosoric and Popovic, and after the interview, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I gave the interview and after I told Colonel Kosoric to report to me at Krivace, I went back in the direction of Bratunac, but I turned in the direction of Voljevica and took the same route to go back to Pribicevac, the same route I had used to come to the meeting: Bratunac, Voljevica, Sase, Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find Colonel Vicic there?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's where I found Colonel Vicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Vicic report to you about what he had done in the meantime as regards the task that he had been assigned?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He briefed me or reported to me that he had carried out work in the spirit of the order that he had been -- the task that he had been given, and that he had drafted the basic combat documents for the command of the forces that were supposed to engage against Zepa. He also told me that he had been monitoring the preparations of the staff command for the removal of the command to the forward command post in Krivace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this where you -- is this the point from which you went to the new forward command post at Krivace?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at the forward command post at Pribicevac from the meeting in Bratunac, it was around, I think, 1330 or maybe 1400 hours. I stayed there for a while, acquainted myself with what Colonel Vicic had done, we had lunch together, and then we went together to Viogora, where the units were supposed to assemble. This was the assembly area for the units engaged in the operation. We headed towards Viogora on the route Pribicevac, Zeleni Jadar, Srebrenica, Viogora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, there's no need for you to point at the map; it is sufficient for you to name the locations along the route.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to indicate that the part of the route from Srebrenica to Viogora, as I said, Viogora is to the west of Srebrenica, and there is a road leading from Srebrenica-Viogora-Suceska-Derventa to Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you, on your way to Viogora, catch up with the units of the Drina Corps, or in general, where were these units at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when we were just very close to Viogora, we caught up with the -- some of the units that were pulling out from their previous positions. But at the time when we came to the Viogora itself, I was informed that all the units had already gathered in the area, in particular, those units that were conducting attacks from the southern side. That's the 1st Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade and the 1st Battalion and parts of the Milici Light Infantry Brigade, which were cooperating with the 2nd Battalion in gaining control of the Kak feature. The Bratunac Brigade was, at that time, in the course of assembling at its previous position, just like the Milici Brigade, except for the part that took active part in combat. They were assembling at their previous positions while at the same time they provided protection to the Serbian villages towards Milici from the direction of Suceska and Ravni Buljim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find the commanding officers of these units there?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up there, I found Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, then Colonel Andric, Colonel Trivic, and Major Nastic, the commander of the Milici Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you issue any orders to them for the purpose of the next action?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed there for a very short time, and I ordered them to speed up the process of assembling and moving the units in order to execute the next task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about the security or protection for the march route towards the Krivace forward command post?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since Major Nastic was at the meeting in Bratunac and since he had heard the axis along which the forces from Viogora were to organise themselves and to march on the Milici-Vlasenica-Han Pijesak route, immediately upon his return he took appropriate action to secure the Viogora-Derventa road and to facilitate safe and secure passage of units. He told me that the road was completely secured and that his Sapper platoon from the brigade was inspecting the road to check the road for anti-tank mines, and he told me that they had not found any such mines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the units of the Drina Corps, or parts of the Drina Corps, were assembling in the area of the Viogora Mountain. What road will they use -- or rather, who designated the road that they were to use to get to the point where they would be executing their next mission?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic ordered which route should be taken, the march route that was to be taken to the area of deployment or the area of engagement, towards Zepa, of course for those forces that would be carrying out the attack on Zepa from the direction of Han Pijesak. However, I had been thinking ever since that time about many more things, about what the Bratunac and Milici Brigade would be doing, because Colonel Vicic and myself, while we were still at Pribicevac, we had been discussing the possible routes and the forces to be engaged along those routes or axes. That is why the forces of the Zvornik Brigade, of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, the 1st Birac Brigade, were organised, and they marched from Viogora, along Viogora-Suceska-Derventa-Milici-Vlasenica-Han Pijesak-Plane. As regards the Milici Brigade and the Bratunac Brigade and the Skelani battalion, the order was that, taking all safety precautions, they should assemble and go to the wider area of Podravanje, Bracani and Rudnik -- or, I'm sorry, the bauxite mine. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. As regards the Bratunac Brigade, the Milici Brigade and the Skelani Battalion, the assembly area that was designated to them was the wider area from Ravani, Bracani, and Rupovo Brdo. This is the area here. And they were to bring in their units using the route Pribicevac-Zeleni Jadar-Kostur-Podravanje. This is part of the Bratunac Brigade and the Skelani Battalion too. As regards the Milici Brigade, it was using the known routes Derventa-Besica Brdo-bauxite mines-Rupovo Brdo. But I already mentioned that they had a lot of work to do to ensure the safety both of their units and of the population there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence would like to stop here, and we suggest that we have the lunch break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. We will have our one-hour break at this point. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.16 p.m. ---

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, before the break, you talked about the Bratunac Brigade, the Milici Brigade, and the Skelani Independent Battalion and their assembly area. Why this area, the area of the Podravanje-Bracani-Rupovo Brdo is a different area from the area in which other units taking part or preparing for the combat operations against Zepa are being assembled?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done for the following reason: When I was with Colonel Vicic at the Pribicevac command post after my return from the meeting from Bratunac, I discussed the grouping of forces with him in view of the task that we had been given, the task that had to do with Zepa, and we defined the forces that would take part in the operation and the axes along which they would attack, and also the assembly areas the attacks were to be against Zepa. So for these three units, so for the Bratunac Brigade, the Milici Brigade, and the Independent Skelani Battalion, the wider assembly area of Podravanje, Rupovo Brdo, and Bracan was determined because in the execution of the task on Zepa, they would be attacking along the line of Podravanje-Orlov Kamen, which is not on this map, Zlovrh and on to Zepa. So that was the main and the only reason for which I assigned this assembly area for these units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this an order that was issued to these units?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time, the order had not yet been issued to these units, but as I passed through the Viogora area, I conveyed all this, communicated all this, to Major Nastic, and he was to communicate this to Colonel Blagojevic. And later on, we will see that when they gathered at the Krivace forward command post, that I did issue that order to the brigade commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go after this assembly was over, and can you describe the routes that you took -- you don't need to show us on the map -- and where did you arrive? What happened, briefly, on that day? I think it's the 12th.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is still the 12th of July, 1995. After a brief stay at the Viogora mountain with the commanders I encountered there, I, together with Colonel Vicic, went on to Vlasenica to the command post. We took the route Viogora-Suceska-Derventa-Milici-Vlasenica. We arrived in Vlasenica sometime between 17 and 1800 hours on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, did you arrive at the command post in Vlasenica, you mean the Drina Corps command post?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, the Drina Corps command post in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom did you find there at the command post?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the command post in Vlasenica, I'd say that the situation there was business as usual. I did not notice any increased presence of officers. I did not go to all of the offices of the organs of the command to determine in any way which of the officers were present there, but in the operations room I did find the duty operations officer of the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he brief you or submit any kind of report to you?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that, on that day, as far as I can remember, the duty operations officer was Colonel Jocic, Predrag Jocic. He was also from the corps staff in the operations and training section. He was there as the duty officer on that day. He gave me a brief report about the situation in the corps, in particular as regards the area of responsibility of the corps, which I had not visited for several days. He said that in the Romanija plateau, which is an area on -- in the direction of Sarajevo from Vlasenica where the forces of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade were defending their positions against Kladanj and Orlovo, and the 1st Podrinje Brigade from Rogatica towards Gorazde and Zepa, that there were no particular developments there except for an attempted attack using the forces from Orlovo at the Orlovo-Sokolac axis. But the attack was successfully repelled. He also told me that between the 11th and the 12th July, the 28th Division had managed to break through in the area between Nova Kasaba, Konjevic Polje, Kravice, and Glogova, and that these forces are headed towards Tuzla, mostly towards the Zvornik Brigade, and partly towards the Birac Brigade, the 1st Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the Vlasenica command post, did you encounter General Zivanovic there?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come that the report was submitted to you by the duty operations officer? Was this in accordance with the rules?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the rule. It was his duty to monitor the situation in the area of responsibility of the corps and to take appropriate measures that are within his jurisdiction. The problems that he is unable to solve, of course, he has to report to the superior officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After his report, did you take any measures in light of his report?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not take any measures to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In light of the situation, was there any indication that the combat operations against Zepa would be cancelled, aborted?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no indications. I did not get any signals from anyone that it was possible, that there was any possibility that the operation against Zepa would be postponed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your opinion in this respect?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion in this respect was similar to the way that Colonel Pandurevic reacted at the meeting at the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade. If I were in General Mladic's shoes, I would not have issued such an order because we did not know where the 28th Division was and what it could do. It would have been much more useful and efficient for the forces that had taken part in the operation in Srebrenica, after their entry into Srebrenica, to go on looking for the 28th Division, to pursue those units, and to get into contact with them in order to avoid the problems that occurred later and which had serious consequences for the 1st Zvornik Brigade and partly for the 1st Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the corps command?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed there for a very short time. After I received the report from the duty operations officer, I personally carried out some preparations for my departure for Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Colonel Vicic with you there?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Colonel Vicic was with me. In addition to carrying out these preparations, I also ordered him draft the text and to prepare a graphic overview of the documents regarding the Zepa operation, as we have agreed at the Pribicevac forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go after you left Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I left Vlasenica, I went to Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is still the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the evening of the 12th of July. I went to Han Pijesak to visit my brother and my mother, and then my wife's family in the village of Kusace, near the forward command post at Krivace. The distance is about five to six kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you arrive at Krivace?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I visited my brother and mother. That's the village of Ljeskovac, four kilometres to the south of Han Pijesak. Then this is the village of Kusace, further down the road, where my wife's family live. That's near the road Han Pijesak-Pozeplje-Zepa. The village of Krivace -- that was the forward command post of the Drina Corps -- is on the eastern slopes of the Zep Mountain, immediately to the east, and the forward command post was between the feature itself and the village of Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I apologise for interrupting, but we never got an answer to the question that was posed by my colleague. The question was: When did you arrive at Krivace? And we still have not heard the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That was my next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you arrive at the forward command post at Krivace?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived between 2200 and 2300 hours at the forward command post, after having spent quite some time with my brother, my mother, and my wife's family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: What was going on at the forward command post and where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quite late at night already. I just came to the forward command post. I saw several soldiers from the staff command, from the battalion -- from the communications battalion. The others were all asleep because they did not get any sleep the night before. They were all very tired. After that, on my way back from the forward command post at Krivace, I went through Plane, where I saw elements of the units that were arriving there and assembling there. After that I went to my in-laws' in the Kusace village and I spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now we go on to the 13th of July. What happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, after I had spent the night, I went straight to the forward command post at Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask the usher to place the Prosecution Exhibit 483 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, General, you arrive at Krivace. Where did you go after that that morning?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had arrived at the Krivace forward command post, I established what the situation was at the forward command post, what its capacity was to be used as the command and control post before the actual beginning of the operations. At the Krivace forward command post I found Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric; Lieutenant Colonel Jevitski; Major Jevdjevic; the commander of the staff command, Lieutenant Amovic; and the soldier of the communications battalion and the staff command. After I had made a tour of the post, I went back and proceeded on to Vlasenica, to the command post in Vlasenica, in order to establish how far Colonel Vicic had gone in his drafting of the combat document, and also in order to take him back to the Krivace forward command post. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you find there at the Vlasenica command post?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Vlasenica command post, like on the previous day, I found the duty officers, the operations duty officer, a number of other officers, and a number of civilians who were there as part of their military obligation. After a while, General Mladic arrived, together with General Zivanovic, from the direction of Bratunac and Milici, and upon their arrival, General Mladic orders that all of the officers and civilian employees who were there should assemble, the people who were there in the corridor of the Corps command. He asked me about the preparations for the Zepa operation, and after I told him that the preparations were underway and that it was possible to proceed with the attack that had been ordered by him, he spoke to the officers and civilian employees who were there. He congratulated them on the success of the Drina Corps units in the Srebrenica operation, and he told me, "Krstic, you are the commander of the forces engaged towards Zepa." So he told me, actually, the same thing, the same thing that he had ordered me in Bratunac: "Until the completion of the Zepa operation, you should not be coming back to the Vlasenica command post."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, after he had spoken those words, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, together with Colonel Vicic but in two separate vehicles, we set off in the direction of Han Pijesak. Together with Lieutenant Savic who also went with me, I went to the hospital of the Main Staff in Sokolac to visit the wounded there. As for Colonel Vicic, he continued to the Krivace forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to the Sokolac military hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed for about one hour at the Sokolac military hospital. I visited the wounded, and I left the hospital after that, together with Lieutenant Savic. And on the way to Sokolac from Han Pijesak, we passed through the village of Sokolovici, Sokolac-Han Pijesak. So on my return journey from Sokolac towards Han Pijesak, we stopped at the village of Sokolovici where Lieutenant Savic's mother lived. So we went to his mother's place; we had lunch together, and thereafter I returned to the Krivace forward command post. We stayed at his mother's for about one hour, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours of the 13th of July -- actually, I should like you to tell us the time when you left the Sokolac military hospital and came to the Krivace forward command post, having passed through the village of Sokolovici.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After our visit to the village of Sokolovici, together with Lieutenant Savic, I visited my in-laws in the Kusace village. We had coffee there. We stayed there for a short time, and after that, I went to the Krivace forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the time it was?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was sometime between 17 and 1800 hours that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do once you arrived --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. It's unclear to me whether the last answer related to the time that he visited -- that General Krstic visited his in-laws in the village. The question that was asked at line 14:40:29 was, "On the afternoon of the 13th, could you tell us the time when you left the Sokolac military hospital and came to the Kravica --" I mean, sorry, "the Krivace forward command post." So there's essentially two questions what time in there: What time did he leave the Sokolac hospital, and what time did he arrive at the forward command post at Krivace. And I don't know if the answer that was offered by General Krstic is responsive to that or to the time that he left and visited his in-laws in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat my question. Yes, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, I think that we need some clarification. I think it is always possible to clear up any misunderstanding. General Krstic said that he had arrived at Krivace around 17 or 1800 hours, but before that, they had had lunch in the village of Sokolovici at the place of the mother of one of his officers. We have two places here, and we need to know the time. If you can help us with that, please, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you perhaps remember the time when you left the Sokolac military hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I'm talking about the 13th of July, after I had left Vlasenica together with Lieutenant Savic and went to the military hospital of the general staff. That happened on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, General, but could you be more specific. Could you tell us the time of date or the hour of the day when you left the Sokolac military hospital and went to the village of Sokolovici?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was sometime between 14 and 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question is, what was the time when you left the village of Sokolovici and went to the forward command post in Krivace?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we had spent one hour with the mother of Lieutenant Savic, we left for the village of Kusace to see my in-laws, so this could have been sometime around 1600 hours. We stayed there for a short period of time on that same day in the village of Kusace, and we finally arrived at the Krivace forward command post between 17 and 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that the issue has been clarified with respect of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So General, finally, you reach the forward command post. What do you do then? Who do you find at the forward command post, and what is the situation there at Krivace?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at the Krivace forward command post, the place was fully functional, and it was possible to exert command and control from that post. And I received a report by Major Jevdjevic to that effect and also by the commander of the staff command, Lieutenant Amovic. Together with Colonel Vicic, once again I had a look at the documents that had been prepared by Colonel Vicic in the meantime, and after that we called -- that is, Colonel Vicic had already told the brigade commanders to come to the forward command post in order to receive their assignments and to execute a command reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have an exhibit in front of you, the Exhibit P483, which was issued by the Drina Corps command and bears the number 02/04-158-1 of the 13th of July 1995. Is this an order, that is, is this order the document that Colonel Vicic worked on together with yourself as part of the preparation activities for the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document in question, and that is the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, General, was it handed over to the unit commanders, and if so, to which units and what units were to take part in the operations that would start the next day?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the brigade commanders arrived at the forward command post, they were given this order for the Zepa operation, which had the secret codename "Stupcanica 95." The order was given to the following commanders: the commander of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade, the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, commander of the Birac Infantry Brigade, commander of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, commander of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, commander of the 5th Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, commander of the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, commander of the 1st Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade, and the commander of the 5th Mixed Artillery Regiment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pursuant to this order, did parts of the basic units of these brigades take part in the operation, and what was the strength of those units that were engaged in this operation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade and the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, which were engaged in their entirety in this operation, as far as other brigades are concerned, only certain elements of those brigades took part, whereas the main body of their forces of these brigades were still deployed along the front line towards Tuzla, Zivinice, Kladanj, Orlovo, and Gorazde. So as regards these brigades, I think that some 20 per cent of the overall strength of those brigades was engaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we are talking about 20 per cent of those brigades, so that 20-per-cent portion of the brigade was commanded by the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, isn't that somewhat illogical, in view of the fact that the major part of the said units had remained at their defensive lines? Who commanded them?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seen from the military perspective, that is entirely logical, because we are talking about offensive activities here. It is correct that the main body of forces of these particular units are in their original areas, securing defence of those areas, and they were commanded by the Chiefs of Staff of these brigades. The officers in question are very experienced officers with many years of experience on their post. They were always ready to replace the brigade commander at any point in time. Furthermore, they were commanding the forces who had been at their defensive positions, at their defensive lines, ever since the beginning of the conflict. So we are talking about very well-fortified lines. So for these reasons, this set-up is not illogical at all, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, if I'm not mistaken, that the Milici and Bratunac Brigades -- strike that. Could you tell us the whereabouts of these two brigades?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade and the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade are still assembling in the area that was -- that had been ordered to them as the starting point to execute their task as part of the Zepa operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they complete or did they arrive in parts?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for these two brigades -- these two brigades were completely engaged in the execution of their assignment towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this order that you yourself prepared, on page 2, paragraph 7, the text is as follows: The first Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade was supposed to detach a unit to the strength of a company which would be made part of the Milici Brigade and carry out assignments, the same assignments that were given to the Milici Light Infantry Brigade, and that they should report to the commander of the Milici Brigade in the area of Bracani by 1800 hours on the 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the situation in which the Milici Brigade had found itself. I have already spoken about the problems this brigade was faced with regarding infiltration and sabotage activities in its rear. It had to be reinforced with one company from the Bratunac Brigade in order to successfully conduct the search of the terrain in the depth of its area of responsibility, and it was later engaged in an attack on the wider frontage towards Zepa. As I already said, it had to be reinforced because of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go back to the same order, page 3, paragraph 9, item C. Mention is made of units that were supposed to cooperate with the MUP. General, could you give us your comment or your analysis of the assignments, if any, that were given to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are not talking about engaging these forces but about a cooperation with the MUP forces that had been deployed for the purposes of the Zepa operation. The area in question is deep in the area of responsibility, which was west to the Zepa enclave, towards Han Pijesak and Vlasenica. It is true that the MUP is mentioned here, and as I have already stated, those were its common assignments: to protect the villages or certain facilities, communication lines, and other features and facilities that were essential for the life and work of the population in a given area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This order, at least in its introductory part -- or let me rephrase the question. Was this order forwarded to the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except for the brigades that can be found in the title of the document, no, the order was not forwarded to these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence should like to suggest that we break at this point and continue tomorrow. I hope that tomorrow we will be able to proceed at somewhat faster pace. And I cannot promise that we will be able to complete the testimony, but on the next day I'm sure -- on the day after that I'm sure that we will be able to finish the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. Thank you. It's always good to hear good intentions and wishes. Let me just remind you that you said that you would need 15 hours for the examination-in-chief. You said that it might take a little longer. But let me just tell you that the 15 hours will soon expire, so you should perhaps speed up with your examination. But, of course, it is really up to you to decide. We will adjourn for the day and come back tomorrow morning at 20 past 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
